rules.title: Answer first
rules.what: Lead with the answer or the result. No greeting, no statement of intent, no restated question.
rules.why: Openers and announcements are generated, transferred and read for nothing; the reader looks for the result first.
rules.how: First sentence = the result, the fix or the decision. Reasoning after, next step last.

verify.how: The first sentence of the reply carries the answer.

rules.title: Say it once
rules.what: State each fact once. Repeat only what safety or understanding needs.
rules.why: A repeated fact costs tokens twice and dilutes what is new.
rules.how: Keep a repetition only for a warning before an irreversible step or a precondition the reader must not miss.

verify.how: No fact is restated in the same reply without a safety reason.

rules.title: Short, never ambiguous
rules.what: Short sentences, precise standard terms. Clarity wins over word count.
rules.why: A shortcut that allows two readings costs a follow-up exchange, which outweighs the words saved.
rules.how: One idea per sentence, active voice, standard acronyms only; write the full sentence when a fragment could be misread.

verify.how: No sentence of the reply allows two readings.

rules.title: No closing recap
rules.what: Stop once the answer is delivered: no summary of what the diff or the output already shows, no offer of more help.
rules.why: A closing recap repeats what the reader just saw, at full token cost.
rules.how: End on the last useful fact or the next step. The bilan of NR-TOK-030 replaces any recap after a task.

verify.how: The reply ends without restating its content.

rules.title: Length follows the question
rules.what: A simple question gets a few lines; a design decision or a risk gets the explanation it needs.
rules.why: Uniform length wastes tokens on simple questions and starves complex ones.
rules.how: Size the reply to the decision the reader must take, not to a habit.

verify.how: Reply length is proportionate to the request.

rules.title: Quiet tool runs
rules.what: No text between routine tool calls. Speak at a phase change, a blocker or the result.
rules.why: Running commentary between read_file, grep and bash calls is output nobody needs.
rules.how: One line before a multi-step run if useful, one line per phase change, one line with the result.

verify.how: Messages between tool calls mark phases, blockers or results only.

rules.title: Load what the task needs
rules.what: Start from the files the task names. Never read a whole repository or documentation set up front.
rules.why: Context is reprocessed on every exchange of the turn: what enters early is paid many times.
rules.how: Read the named files, then follow references; use `select` to load only the relevant rule families.

verify.how: No bulk read of the repository or documentation without a task reason.

rules.title: Search before reading
rules.what: Locate with grep on a symbol, name or message, then read the matching range.
rules.why: A targeted search costs a few lines; a full file read costs the whole file, for every later exchange.
rules.how: grep for the symbol or error text, then read_file on the range found.

verify.how: Large files are read by range after a search.

rules.title: Reuse the context
rules.what: Do not reread a file whose content is in context and unchanged since.
rules.why: A second read of the same unchanged content doubles its cost and adds nothing.
rules.how: Reread only after an edit, an external change or a /compact that dropped it.

verify.how: No unchanged file is read twice in the same context.

rules.title: Shrink bulky output
rules.what: Filter logs, JSON, CSV, YAML and test output before it enters the context.
rules.why: Raw logs and full test output fill the context with lines the task does not use.
rules.how: Pipe through tail, grep or jq; keep failures and the decisive error line, drop passing tests and noise.

verify.how: Tool output entering the context is filtered to what the task uses.

rules.title: Compress without loss
rules.what: Any summary keeps errors verbatim, and negations, numbers, units, paths, identifiers, commands and code exactly.
rules.why: A compression that drops a negation or a number produces a wrong fix, then a retry that costs more than the tokens saved.
rules.how: Quote the decisive error line as is; never paraphrase a path, an id, a version or a command.

verify.how: Summaries preserve errors, negations, numbers, units, paths, ids and code.

rules.title: Lean instruction files
rules.what: Keep AGENTS.md and SKILL.md short, each instruction in one place, specialized rules loaded on demand.
rules.why: Instruction files load at every session: each line is paid in every conversation.
rules.how: One line per rule in AGENTS.md; remove what the code already shows; move details to references read on demand.

verify.how: Instruction files carry no duplicate and no detail that belongs in a reference.

rules.title: Details in reference files
rules.what: Move long references to files read on demand, out of the instructions loaded every session.
rules.why: A reference used once a month should not be paid in every session.
rules.how: Keep the trigger in the skill or AGENTS.md, the content in references/ or docs/.

verify.how: Long references live in files loaded on demand.

rules.title: Nothing off-task in context
rules.what: Drop unrelated results, generated files, lockfiles and minified bundles before they reach the model.
rules.why: Off-task content costs tokens and attention, and misleads the next step.
rules.how: Exclude build output, vendored code and lockfiles from searches; do not @-mention files the task does not touch.

verify.how: No generated, vendored or unrelated content entered the context.

rules.title: Cause before code
rules.what: Reproduce or locate the cause before editing. Do not chain trial fixes on unverified guesses.
rules.why: Each trial fix is a full edit, test and reread cycle; a located cause usually needs one.
rules.how: Read the error, reproduce it, find the line; state the hypothesis and check it before editing.

verify.how: Each fix follows a cause that was located or reproduced.

rules.title: Targeted edits
rules.what: Edit the lines that change. Never rewrite a whole file to fix a few lines.
rules.why: A full rewrite generates the whole file and risks regressions far from the fix.
rules.how: Use edit on the precise range; write_file only for a new file or a real rewrite.

verify.how: The diff touches only the lines the change needs.

rules.title: Show only the change
rules.what: Show the changed lines with minimal context, or cite file:line. Print a whole file only on request.
rules.why: Reprinting an unchanged file generates and displays tokens the reader already has.
rules.how: Cite path:line, show the diff hunk, link to the file.

verify.how: Replies show diffs or references, not whole unchanged files.

rules.title: Reuse existing tools
rules.what: Run the project's scripts, tests and commands before writing an equivalent.
rules.why: A rewritten tool costs generation, review and maintenance; the existing one is already trusted.
rules.how: Look for make targets, package scripts and validators first; run them and read their output.

verify.how: No new script duplicates an existing project command.

rules.title: No call with a known result
rules.what: Do not rerun a search, command or test whose output cannot have changed.
rules.why: A repeated call costs a round trip and its output tokens for nothing new.
rules.how: Rerun only after a change that can affect the result; do not poll, wait for the result.

verify.how: No identical call is repeated without an intervening change.

rules.title: Batch independent calls
rules.what: Send independent reads, searches and commands in one round. Keep dependent steps in sequence.
rules.why: Each round trip reprocesses the context; batching independent calls saves rounds.
rules.how: Group independent read_file and grep calls; keep sequence where a result feeds the next call.

verify.how: Independent calls are grouped; dependent ones stay ordered.

rules.title: Proportionate checks
rules.what: Run the tests closest to the change first; widen when the risk or the dependencies call for it.
rules.why: A full suite on every small edit costs time and output; skipping checks costs rework.
rules.how: Run the test file of the change, then the suite before commit or when shared code moved.

verify.how: The tests run match the scope and risk of the change.

rules.title: Stop at done
rules.what: Stop once the acceptance criteria pass. No unrequested feature, refactoring or cleanup.
rules.why: Out-of-scope work costs tokens, review time and regression risk the user did not ask for.
rules.how: Name the done-criteria at the start; stop and report when they pass; propose extras in one line.

verify.how: The change contains nothing beyond the acceptance criteria.

rules.title: Model sized to the task
rules.what: Use a lighter model or a lower thinking level for simple work, the heaviest for hard problems.
rules.why: A large model on a mechanical task spends computation the task does not need.
rules.how: Switch with /model and lower /thinking for routine work; point [utility_models] to a small model.

verify.how: The model and thinking level match the task's difficulty.

rules.title: No heavy call for light work
rules.what: Do not spend a large model or a subagent on what a command, a script or a lookup answers.
rules.why: A subagent or a large model call costs a full context for an answer a command gives in one line.
rules.how: grep, a script or the validator first; the task tool for wide read-only scans only.

verify.how: No model or subagent call replaces a deterministic command.

rules.title: Deterministic work stays local
rules.what: Filter, sort, format, validate syntax and compute with local tools.
rules.why: A local tool gives an exact result at a fraction of the computation of model reasoning.
rules.how: jq, sort, a linter, a formatter or a short script; the model interprets the output.

verify.how: Mechanical operations ran through local tools.

rules.title: Use the cache
rules.what: Reuse cached results and keep prompt prefixes stable while the data and the conditions stay valid.
rules.why: Cached prefixes and results avoid recomputing what has not changed.
rules.how: Keep AGENTS.md and system instructions stable within a session; reuse validated artifacts instead of regenerating them.

verify.how: Stable content is reused rather than regenerated.

rules.title: Quality first
rules.what: No saving justifies a loss of security, correctness, accessibility, maintainability or clarity. In a conflict, quality wins.
rules.why: A cheap but wrong or inaccessible result costs a full rework, and harms people.
rules.how: When brevity and quality conflict, keep the check, the warning or the explanation.

verify.how: No security, correctness, accessibility or clarity was traded for tokens.

rules.title: Measure, never estimate
rules.what: When the client reports them, record input, output and cache tokens, calls and cost against an equivalent baseline.
rules.why: An estimated saving is a fabricated number; a measured one can be compared.
rules.how: Use the token usage Vibe reports when it is available; for headless runs, --output json and --max-tokens; compare like with like.

verify.how: Any saving quoted comes from a measurement against a baseline.

limits: Direction (fewer tokens -> less compute -> less energy) holds; any token-to-energy ratio depends on caching, model and hardware: measure before quoting numbers.

rules.title: Count the whole run
rules.what: Include retries, errors, fixes and rework. A short reply that needs a second attempt costs more than a complete one.
rules.why: Token sobriety is a property of the whole run, not of one message.
rules.how: Judge an optimisation on the run: tokens, calls and retries until done.

verify.how: Optimisations are judged on the whole run including retries.

rules.title: Report what was applied
rules.what: After a task that ran tools or changed files, add the token sobriety block to the bilan. Skip it for a plain question. Never invent a metric.
rules.why: The report makes the practice visible and checkable; an invented number destroys that trust.
rules.how: List the NR-TOK ids applied, the actions, the measures Vibe reported or 'non disponible', the tests and the limits.

verify.how: The bilan carries the NR-TOK block with no invented metric.
